extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral candidates applying for the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation (HHWF) Research Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility rules for applicants to the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation Research Fellowship, covering who may apply, application components, institutional/visa issues, stipend/policy rules, and in-fellowship changes. Intended to help prospective postdoctoral applicants complete and update their applications and understand program constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral laboratory tenure limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation accepts applications from candidates who have been working in their postdoctoral laboratory for no more than one year at the time of the deadline for submitting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This one-year limit allows time to finish work in the thesis laboratory and to submit/revise papers. The Foundation may, at its discretion, accept applications where postdoctoral research has extended a month or two longer than the one-year limit but will not approve substantially longer intervals. Clinical residencies, military service, parental leaves, etc., are not considered postdoctoral research experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD and MD degree date limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have received a PhD (or D.Phil. or equivalent) no more than two years before the application deadline, or an M.D. degree no more than four years before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The day you defend your thesis is considered the Ph.D. date; an M.D. date is the formal awarding date of the degree. The Foundation may allow a short (month or two) extension at its discretion but not substantially longer intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply before degree awarded
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply before obtaining your degree as long as you will receive your degree before you intend to start your postdoctoral research under a Whitney Fellowship grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting non-academic/industry time toward limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Time spent working at a biotech company counts as part of the two-year maximum between thesis defense and the application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD/PhD recency rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant obtains both an M.D. and a Ph.D., the Foundation uses the most recently obtained degree to evaluate the time-limit eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, eligibility depends on whether the most recent degree was obtained within the allowed time window and on not having more than one year of postdoctoral research experience by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution type acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation expects fellowship training to be obtained in an academic setting, but non-profit research institutes (privately or publicly supported) are appropriate places for HHWF postdoctoral training; federal government research institutions (e.g., NIH) are also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When awarded at NIH, HHWF pays the fellow directly on a quarterly basis and issues a Federal Form-1099; the research allowance is paid directly to the NIH. For non-governmental institutions, stipends are normally issued semi-annually to the university or research institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple fellows in same laboratory
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of one Whitney Fellow in the laboratory of your prospective sponsor will not adversely affect your application; the Foundation does award up to two Whitney Fellows in the same lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You may reapply a second time as long as you do not have more than one year of postdoctoral experience by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each year a revised online application form is created; if you reapply, use the new one. You must reapply as if you never applied before and cannot reactivate your old application. The Foundation cautions that reapplying may not be worth the effort unless your credentials have substantially changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention / patent citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not maintain an invention/patent policy; the only stipulation is that fellows cite the HHWF in any publications or discoveries resulting from the Whitney Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution invention/patent policies will likely apply to the fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and single-lab commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship is a three-year commitment for one laboratory only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unusual circumstances arise (mentor moves, spousal move, etc.), a transfer request may be made and is subject to review and approval by the SAC Chairman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab transfer / change during fellowship process
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-fellowship requests to transfer to another laboratory or institution are considered but require review by the SAC Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair generally requires an outline of the proposed project in the new lab, a letter from the new sponsor, and when appropriate a short note of approval from the current sponsor. In most past cases (mentor moves, spousal move, mutual agreement that another lab is more appropriate), approval has been straightforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: No overhead on stipend or research allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of the research allowance can be used for overhead; this policy extends to the fellowship stipend as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of equipment purchased with research allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Portable equipment purchased with the research allowance, such as laptops, may be kept by the fellow after finishing the fellowship; fixed lab equipment remains in the lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter source acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference letters should be from referees closely familiar with you and your work; collaboration-based familiarity is acceptable so long as the referee knows you well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the instructions refer to letters ‘from three of your former professors or supervisors’, the Foundation emphasizes that closeness of knowledge is the key criterion for acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective supervisor and sponsor letters vs. reference letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include your prospective supervisor as a reference; the prospective supervisor may provide a sponsor's letter commenting on you and your work but because of potential conflict of interest the Foundation focuses more on the evaluation from the other reference letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation requires 4 other reference letters, one of which should be from your thesis advisor; the sponsor’s letter is separate from these references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-supervisors allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible to have two co-supervisors for the Fellowship when work is interdisciplinary and both have relevant expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter both names in the application and assign roles as ‘Prospective Supervisor’ (primary) or ‘Secondary Supervisor’ using the drop-down menu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-page research proposal balance guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 5-page research proposal, applicants should balance background/relevance versus experimental detail appropriately for their project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no rigid guidelines beyond the instructions. Assume reviewers will be experts in your broad field (e.g., neuroscience, structural biology, developmental biology) but not necessarily specialists in your specific topic—choose a balance suitable for that audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating application with newly accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper cited in your bibliography is accepted after you applied, you may submit it to the Foundation to update your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email the accepted paper to the provided HHWF contact email and they will update your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign applicants — visa documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants must obtain appropriate visa documentation as required by U.S. Immigration, but it is sufficient to state intent to obtain the visa in time for the fellowship activation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this statement as a separate letter in your application and when uploading select 'Miscellaneous Letter' from the drop-down menu. The Foundation does not specify which visa a fellow must obtain; fellows must comply with U.S. immigration laws and institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social security number field for non-US applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not a U.S. citizen and do not have a social security number, enter 'NA' in that field on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI‑Janelia Research Campus special-case handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from candidates planning to do postdoctoral research at the Janelia Research Campus are accepted and given the same consideration as others even if Janelia's policy prevents receiving external funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awarded and stipend must be declined, stipend salary would be paid directly by HHMI. Fellows from Janelia are otherwise treated identically, including participation in Annual Fellow’s Meetings.
